description:
Repros (elixir prints the value shown):
- Enum.to_list(Stream.map([fn x -> x end], fn f -> f.(1) end))   # [1]; scratchpad handoff/closure_elem.fz
- No Stream, 5 lines (scratchpad s131/min.fz, prints 1):
    defmodule M do
      def ap([], e), do: e
      def ap([f | r], e), do: f.(ap(r, e))
    end
    IO.inspect(M.ap([fn f -> f.(1) end], fn x -> x end))
  M.ap(f, e) without the list recursion passes; the recursion that makes ap return a union is needed.

On 3038a76af both stop first at the boxed-apply lane check ("expects delivered lane(s) [] but construction wrapper publishes [ValueRef]"). That check misfires on a call that never returns and is fixed by fz-sc8.147.

What remains here, seen with the fz-sc8.147 change applied (verified location, cause inferred):
- interp: "backend continuation delivery executable=... entry=2: backend return layout decoded 0 lane(s), got 1"
- run: "native cannot project captures out of a callable that names no function in Continuation { owner: FnId(N) }"
The failing continuation is entry 2 of M.ap with inputs [a0_e], a1. Its expected layout is carrier Absent, 0 lanes, shape Callable(CallableId(0)), a statically zero-lane callable; the delivered value is a heap closure that encodes as one lane. One half treats the closure as a statically known zero-capture callable and the other passes the boxed word. The mapper also has a specialization over a free arrow variable (a0) sitting as a diverging member of the wrapper at main's construction site; that may be the root.

Next: find which fact gives the continuation entry its Absent carrier and which gives the delivered value its one lane; fixture with an oracle on all three paths. Blocked on fz-sc8.147.
title: A Stream.map mapper that calls a closure element compiles
